projects.name: Commerce Core
projects.summary: Design a Spring Boot store API with product, inventory, and order flows backed by PostgreSQL.
projects.description: A backend for a small online store: manage a product catalog, keep stock accurate, and let customers place and track orders.
projects.purpose: This project shows how a Java service can connect the main parts of a shopping workflow. It is a sample concept, not a completed or deployed application.
projects.learn: REST API design, relational modeling, transaction boundaries, validation, and cache invalidation.
features: Browse products with search, category filters, and pagination.
Create orders from available stock and calculate totals on the server.
Prevent overselling by changing inventory inside a database transaction.
Track order states such as pending, paid, packed, and shipped.
roadmap: Create a Spring Boot application and define Product, Inventory, Order, and OrderItem models.
Add PostgreSQL with Spring Data JPA and write schema constraints and migrations.
Build validated REST endpoints for catalog, stock, and order workflows.
Add service-layer transactions, global error responses, and unit/integration tests.
Add Redis caching for product reads, Docker Compose for local services, and API documentation.

projects.name: EventFlow
projects.summary: Explore asynchronous order events, retry handling, and independent consumers using Kafka.
projects.description: An order-event pipeline where separate services process confirmations, stock updates, and customer notifications asynchronously.
projects.purpose: This project demonstrates how producers and consumers communicate through events, so slow background work does not block an order API. It is a sample concept, not a running service.
projects.learn: Message-driven architecture, Kafka topics, retries, idempotency, and eventual consistency.
features: Publish an OrderCreated event after an order is accepted.
Use independent consumers for inventory and email tasks.
Retry temporary failures and route repeated failures to a dead-letter topic.
Make event processing idempotent so duplicate messages do not duplicate work.
roadmap: Start a Spring Boot API and Kafka broker locally with Docker Compose.
Define versioned event payloads and an order-created topic.
Publish events only after database commits using an outbox table.
Build separate consumers with retry policies, dead-letter handling, and idempotency.
Add integration tests with a test broker and document how to inspect messages.

projects.name: Stockroom
projects.summary: Build an inventory service with clear CRUD APIs, relational data, validation, and low-stock alerts.
projects.description: An inventory management API for products, stock movements, and low-stock warnings.
projects.purpose: This is a focused way to practice reliable data modeling and CRUD APIs. Every stock change is recorded so an operator can understand when and why inventory changed.
projects.learn: Relational modeling, validation, transactional updates, audit history, and pagination.
features: Create and update products with SKU and category validation.
Record stock additions, removals, and corrections as auditable movements.
Reject changes that would leave stock below zero.
Filter inventory and identify products below their reorder threshold.
roadmap: Model Product, Category, and StockMovement entities with clear relationships.
Create a MySQL schema with unique SKU and non-negative quantity constraints.
Implement DTO-based REST APIs and request validation.
Use transactions for stock movements and add service and repository tests.
Add pagination, sorting, OpenAPI docs, and a Docker-based local setup.

projects.name: ShipShape
projects.summary: Prototype a repeatable delivery pipeline for a containerized Java service deployed to AWS.
projects.description: A repeatable build-and-deploy pipeline for a containerized Spring Boot service running in AWS.
projects.purpose: The goal is to make releases predictable: code changes run tests and produce a versioned container before deployment. This is a sample delivery project, not a live cloud deployment.
projects.learn: CI/CD pipelines, containerization, cloud configuration, secrets handling, and deployment checks.
features: Build and test on every pull request.
Create a small production-ready Docker image.
Store runtime configuration outside the application image.
Deploy to an AWS EC2 instance and expose a health check.
roadmap: Prepare a small Spring Boot API with tests and an Actuator health endpoint.
Write a multi-stage Dockerfile and run the container locally.
Add GitHub Actions workflow steps for build, tests, and image creation.
Configure AWS credentials as repository secrets and provision an EC2 host.
Deploy the versioned image, verify health, and document rollback and cleanup.

projects.name: QuickCache
projects.summary: Learn cache-aside patterns, expiry, and invalidation for frequently requested catalog data.
projects.description: A product-catalog service that speeds up repeated reads with a Redis cache in front of PostgreSQL.
projects.purpose: This project makes caching behavior visible: measure repeated reads, set an expiry policy, and keep cached data consistent after an update. It is a sample concept.
projects.learn: Cache-aside design, TTL, invalidation, performance measurement, and consistency trade-offs.
features: Cache frequently requested product details by ID.
Use a time-to-live to limit stale values.
Evict or refresh cache entries when a product changes.
Compare response time and database access with caching enabled and disabled.
roadmap: Build catalog endpoints and persist product data in PostgreSQL.
Add Redis locally with Docker Compose and configure Spring Cache.
Cache read operations with a clear key and expiry policy.
Invalidate cache entries on create, update, and delete operations.
Add tests for cache hits, expiration, and invalidation; document trade-offs.

projects.name: SecureGate
projects.summary: Practice secure REST endpoints with authentication, role-based access, and token validation.
projects.description: A secured REST API with user sign-in, token-based authentication, and role-based permissions.
projects.purpose: This project is for practicing the boundaries between authentication and authorization: identify a user safely, then allow only the actions their role permits. It is a learning concept, not a production security product.
projects.learn: Authentication, authorization, password hashing, token lifecycle, and security testing.
features: Register and authenticate users with password hashes.
Issue and validate short-lived JWT access tokens.
Protect endpoints by role and ownership rules.
Return consistent authorization errors without exposing secrets.
roadmap: Create User and Role models and store password hashes using a strong encoder.
Configure Spring Security filter chains and public versus protected routes.
Implement login and token validation with a maintained JWT library.
Add role checks, ownership checks, input validation, and security-focused tests.
Document token expiry and secret configuration; never commit signing secrets.
